docRequirement: model-config.md:454 — "The default effort is `high` on every model that supports effort, except Opus 4.7, which defaults to `xhigh`." The default is therefore a per-model fact, not one value. model-config.md:456 adds the hold: "When you first run Fable 5, Opus 4.8, or Opus 4.7, Claude Code applies that model's default effort even if you previously set a different level for another model, and holds it across sessions until you make an explicit effort choice, such as running `/effort` in an interactive session or launching with `--effort`. Opus 5 has no such hold." model-config.md:506 fixes where that default sits in precedence: "The environment variable takes precedence over all other methods, then your configured level, then the model default."

DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL` and takes no model argument at all. divergence:
Two deltas, and neither is a key-name mismatch — the value is wrong AND the model id is never an input.

1. `:454` value/axis. Every effort-capable model defaults to `medium` here; the page requires `high` on all of them and `xhigh` on Opus 4.7. There is no per-model table, no `defaultEffort` on `ModelDefinition`, and no model parameter on `resolveEffortLevel`. `clampThinkingLevelToModel` is model-aware but is the wrong rule: it narrows a chosen level and never supplies one.

2. `:456` hold — not built at all. The persisted level cannot distinguish "the user chose this" from "this was inherited" (`config.defaultThinkingLevel` is one string written by `setDefaultThinkingLevel`, packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:2495-2502), so there is nothing to hold and nothing to release, and a switch to Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 silently carries the previous model's level over.

One structural consequence for the fix: `:506` puts the model default BELOW the configured level, but our chain terminates at `getDefaultThinkingLevel()`, which always returns a concrete value. A model default inserted underneath it would be dead code unless the shipped config default is made distinguishable from a real user choice.

change.what: Add a per-model default table as a sibling of `NARROWED_EFFORT_MODELS` (:220-225) plus `export function getModelDefaultThinkingLevel(modelId: string): ThinkingLevel | undefined`. Entries: /claude[-.]opus-4-7/i -> 'xhigh'; /claude[-.](opus-4-8|sonnet-5|sonnet-4-6|opus-4-6|fable-5)/i -> 'high'. Match bare, slash-prefixed and Bedrock-native (`us.anthropic.claude-…`) id forms exactly as :224 already does. Scope it deliberately to the ids model-config.md:446-450 tables: an absent entry returns `undefined` so unlisted Pi/gateway models keep `DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL` — the same 'not known to be different' convention the file already documents at :217-219. Do NOT fold this into `resolveEffortLevel`'s body; the comment at :190-199 exists because merging the narrowing rule into the choosing rule broke it once. Callers pass it as `fallback:` instead.

Split it. Add `export function getConfiguredDefaultThinkingLevel(): ThinkingLevel | undefined` returning ONLY the user-set `config.defaultThinkingLevel` (normalized), and leave `getDefaultThinkingLevel()` as today's always-concrete shipped fallback for existing callers. Without this split the model default is unreachable, because the current function never returns undefined.

Model-aware terminal fallback. The model is only known after :8913-8934, so compute the level in two steps: keep `normalizeThinkingLevel(options?.thinkingLevel) ?? projectDefaults ?? wsConfig ?? getConfiguredDefaultThinkingLevel()` here, then after `resolvedModel` exists finish with `?? getModelDefaultThinkingLevel(resolvedModel) ?? getDefaultThinkingLevel()`. The single consumer at :9276 (`thinkingLevel: defaultThinkingLevel`) is unchanged. Keep the comment block at :8897-8899 accurate — it currently states a four-tier chain.

Decision point, not a mechanical edit. `"think"` (-> medium) is what makes the model default unreachable through the workspace tier. Option A (recommended, S): leave it and accept that the model default only applies when neither the user nor the workspace set one. Option B (full `/effort auto` parity, model-config.md:499): introduce `"auto"`, which also requires `ConfigDefaults.thinkingLevel` (packages/shared/src/config/config-defaults-schema.ts:44), the validator enum (packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:130) and the in-code mirror `FALLBACK_CONFIG_DEFAULTS` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:189) to accept it. Both files must stay in lockstep — storage.ts:166 says so.

The `:456` hold, the largest piece. Needs two new persisted facts next to `defaultThinkingLevel`: (a) an explicit-choice marker set by every explicit setter — `setDefaultThinkingLevel` here and the session-level setter behind `settings:setDefaultThinkingLevel` — that releases the hold; (b) a per-model first-run record so the first use of `claude-fable-5`, `claude-opus-4-8` or `claude-opus-4-7` applies that model's default once even when a different level is stored. Both are new keys in `~/.nessy-agent/config.json` written through `saveConfig` — a persistence-boundary change, so it needs its own migration-safe read (absent key = no hold in force, i.e. current behaviour).

One positive path (`claude-opus-4-7` -> 'xhigh'; `claude-opus-4-8`/`claude-sonnet-5`/`claude-fable-5` -> 'high') and one negative/boundary (an unlisted gateway id -> undefined, so `resolveEffortLevel` still lands on `DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL`), placed beside the existing clamp cases at :56-79. Add one case proving the model default does NOT override an explicit session/declared/invocation level (model-config.md:506 ordering).

Extend for the getter split: a config with no `defaultThinkingLevel` must make `getConfiguredDefaultThinkingLevel()` return undefined while `getDefaultThinkingLevel()` still returns the shipped value. Two existing mocks pin the old single getter and must keep compiling: apps/electron/src/main/handlers/__tests__/settings-default-thinking.test.ts:8 (mocks `'think'`) and apps/electron/src/main/__tests__/session-branch-rollback.isolated.ts:75 (mocks `'medium'`).

userImpact: Observable today, in a default build. Anthropic models are offered on any Anthropic API-key connection (packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:649,718), so this is not gated behind the opt-in `NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE` subscription flow. Concretely: pick Opus 4.7 and start a new chat — the composer's thinking selector reads the medium level and the request goes out with `effort: 'medium'` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2205 -> packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:234), where Claude Code would run that model at `xhigh`; on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5 and Fable 5 it is `medium` against a documented `high`. The user gets visibly shallower, cheaper reasoning than the same model gives in Claude Code, and nothing in the UI explains the difference. Second, switching a workspace to Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 never bumps the level to that model's default: whatever the previous model was set to carries over silently — exactly the failure `:456`'s hold exists to prevent. Both halves are latent for Pi/Nessy Gateway models, which the page's table does not cover.
notes: The `:454` half alone is M (one table + one getter split + the session-creation chain + tests); the `:456` hold is what makes the whole thing L, because it adds persisted state and needs every explicit-set path to release it. This is a DUPLICATE of an already-recorded deviation, not a new discovery: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:100 and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-effort-precedence.md:180 both carry the identical 'documented, not implemented' string for model-config.md:454/:456 — the spec above is the implementable form of that row, not a new claim. Scoping judgement worth an owner decision before execution: raising the default from `medium` to `high` for every listed Anthropic model is a real token-spend increase, and the fork deliberately runs many unlisted models (Haiku on a fixed token budget, every discovered gateway model) where the page's table says nothing — the recommendation above keeps `DEFAULT_THINKING_LEVEL` for those rather than reading :444 literally, which is the same reasoning the plan already recorded for the clamp table. Also note our `off` level (packages/shared/src/agent/thinking-levels.ts:29) sits below `low` and has no counterpart on this page; it is untouched by this change.
